    "gene": "APP",
    "target_id": "ENSG00000142192",
    "evidence_types": [
      "Human genetics with functional follow-up: APP A673T is associated with protection against Alzheimer disease and cognitive decline in elderly people without Alzheimer disease; in vitro assays show reduced amyloidogenic peptide formation (PMID:22801501). Lifelong genetic protection does not establish efficacy of starting APP suppression after disease onset.",
      "Randomized clinical trial: lecanemab, which targets APP-derived amyloid-beta protofibrils, reduced amyloid burden and moderately slowed cognitive and functional decline in early Alzheimer disease (PMID:36449413). This supports targeting the cleavage product, not direct inhibition of full-length APP."
    ],
    "direction": "Decrease pathogenic APP-derived amyloid-beta burden, preferentially by neutralizing or clearing aggregated amyloid-beta while preserving physiological APP functions. Clinical support is for modest slowing of cognitive and functional decline in amyloid-positive early Alzheimer disease, not cognitive restoration or indiscriminate full-length APP inhibition; anti-amyloid treatment carries ARIA risk."
  },
  {
    "gene": "ACHE",
    "target_id": "ENSG00000087085",
    "evidence_types": [
      "Human randomized clinical trials, synthesized in a systematic review: donepezil, an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, provides small cognitive and functional benefits versus placebo in Alzheimer dementia (PMID:29923184). Trials and their review count as one evidence type; this is symptomatic efficacy, not established disease modification.",
      "Biochemical functional experiments: human recombinant acetylcholinesterase accelerates amyloid-beta fibril assembly through its peripheral binding site; this effect was sensitive to a peripheral-site ligand but not an active-site inhibitor (PMID:8608006). This is mechanistic evidence, not proof that catalytic inhibition modifies disease."

      "Human clinical pharmacology: donepezil, an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, has demonstrated cognitive benefits across Alzheimer disease severity; clinical evidence reviewed in PMID:25690270; DOI:10.1111/ane.12386.",
      "Animal functional pharmacology: in rats, donepezil alone increased extracellular hippocampal acetylcholine and evoked theta/gamma power in a study also testing idalopirdine combinations. These pharmacodynamic endpoints support mechanism, not cognitive efficacy in an Alzheimer disease model; PMID:27039041; DOI:10.1016/j.neuropharm.2016.03.043."
    ],
    "direction": "Inhibit CNS acetylcholinesterase activity to increase synaptic acetylcholine for symptomatic cognitive benefit in Alzheimer dementia. Use tolerable partial inhibition; cholinergic adverse effects, including bradycardia and gastrointestinal effects, constrain dosing. Disease modification is not established."

      "Human molecular imaging: an independent observational MP4A-PET study in clinically diagnosed amnestic MCI or mild Alzheimer dementia linked lower cortical acetylcholinesterase activity to Alzheimer-typical atrophy and hypoperfusion (PMID:40116674).     "direction": "Inhibit acetylcholinesterase enzymatic activity to slow acetylcholine breakdown and enhance residual cholinergic neurotransmission. Established symptomatic strategy; disease modification is not established, and tolerability limits inhibition."
